about: The binding rule (docs/named-result-sets-scope.md, Binding rule and its case table) over SqlScript.Parse and ScriptDom, with no server. slots lists, per batch, the [position, name] pairs the plan names (positions count one batch execution's sets with columns, plans left out). notes lists every static note (unbatched markers first, then each batch's, before it runs), each as a fragment of its text, in order. run, when given, replays one execution of a batch: each set is {columns: n}, with plan: true for a plan set and showplan: true for SHOWPLAN or STATISTICS PROFILE text, and {error: true} is an error raised between sets; names lists the name each set with columns gets (null for none) and unapplied the notes after the execution.

cases.name: named SELECT, then an unnamed SELECT
statements of class None before it do not move it
named statement that returns no set
notes: "Changed" (line 1) is unused: its statement returns no result set.

cases.name: named EXEC that returns three sets: the first is named
cases.sql:
-- #Name="Order"
EXEC dbo.GetOrder @OrderId = 42;

cases.name: three markers stacked before an EXEC that returns three sets
cases.sql:
-- #Name="Order"
-- #Name="Lines"
-- #Name="Totals"
EXEC dbo.GetOrder @OrderId = 42;

cases.name: more stacked markers than sets
cases.sql:
-- #Name="Order"
-- #Name="Lines"
-- #Name="Totals"
EXEC dbo.GetOrder @OrderId = 42;

unapplied: "Totals" (line 3) is unused: its statement returned fewer result sets than there are names.

cases.name: a named EXEC that returns no set

unapplied: "Order" (line 1) is unused: its statement returned no result set.

cases.name: more stacked markers than a SELECT's one set
notes: "Two" (line 2) is unused: its statement returns one result set

cases.name: name before IF: its first set takes it
cases.sql:
-- #Name="Branch"
IF 1 = 1 SELECT 1 AS a; ELSE SELECT 2 AS b;

cases.name: name before WHILE that returns no set
cases.sql:
-- #Name="Loop"
WHILE 1 = 0 SELECT 1 AS a;

unapplied: "Loop" (line 1) is unused: its statement returned no result set.

cases.name: name inside BEGIN ... END
cases.sql:
BEGIN
  -- #Name="Inside"
  SELECT 1 AS a;
END
notes: "Inside" (line 2) was not applied: it is inside a BEGIN … END statement on line 1, where how often

cases.name: name inside a branch
notes: "Branch body" (line 2) was not applied: it is inside an IF statement on line 1

cases.name: name inside a TRY block
cases.sql:
BEGIN TRY
  -- #Name="Tried"
  SELECT 1 AS a;
END TRY
BEGIN CATCH
END CATCH
notes: "Tried" (line 2) was not applied: it is inside a TRY … CATCH statement on line 1

cases.name: name before a UNION branch
cases.sql:
SELECT 1 AS a
UNION ALL
-- #Name="Branch"
SELECT 2;
notes: "Branch" (line 3) was not applied: it is inside a SELECT statement on line 1, not before one.

cases.name: name in a subquery
notes: "Sub" (line 2) was not applied: it is inside a SELECT statement on line 1

cases.name: named statement after an EXEC
notes: "Staged rows" (line 2) was not applied: an EXEC statement on line 1 before it returns an unknown number of result sets. Put GO between them.

cases.name: named statement after an IF
notes: "After" (line 2) was not applied: an IF statement on line 1 before it

cases.name: named EXEC followed by a statement that may return a set
notes: "Order" (line 1) was not applied: a SELECT statement on line 3 after it may also return result sets

cases.name: name at the end of a batch
notes: "Last" (line 2) is unused: no statement follows it in its batch.

cases.name: name in a batch of comments only, and a name never crosses a GO
notes: "Alone" (line 3) is unused: no statement follows it in its batch.

cases.name: the same name twice
GO 3: the batch is planned once and each repetition names its set
a marker in a string or a nested comment names nothing
a selection's lines are counted from its first line
notes: "Changed" (line 11) is unused

cases.name: SET STATISTICS XML ON: plan sets are left out of the count
the batch does not parse
cases.sql:
-- #Name="Broken"
SELECT FROM WHERE;
notes: Result names in the batch starting on line 1 were not applied: the batch does not parse.

cases.name: the second batch does not parse
notes: Result names in the batch starting on line 3 were not applied: the batch does not parse.

cases.name: after the first error in a batch execution no name is applied

unapplied: "B" (line 4) was not applied: an error earlier in its batch made the place of its result set unknown.

cases.name: a set with another column count than its statement selects stops binding

unapplied: "Named" (line 2) was not applied: a result set arrived that its batch's statements do not select
"Later" (line 4) was not applied: a result set arrived

cases.name: SHOWPLAN or STATISTICS PROFILE text stops binding
cases.sql:
-- #Name="Rows"
SELECT * FROM sys.objects;

unapplied: "Rows" (line 1) was not applied: SHOWPLAN or STATISTICS PROFILE output in its batch

cases.name: DML with OUTPUT is named
cases.sql:
-- #Name="Inserted"
INSERT INTO #t (id) OUTPUT inserted.id VALUES (1);

cases.name: DML with OUTPUT INTO returns no set
cases.sql:
-- #Name="Logged"
INSERT INTO #t (id) OUTPUT inserted.id INTO @log (id) VALUES (1);
notes: "Logged" (line 1) is unused: its statement returns no result set.

cases.name: malformed markers name nothing and say nothing
cases.sql:
-- #Name="unclosed
SELECT 1 AS a;

cases.name: a batch with SET NOEXEC applies no name, even before it: an ON from an earlier batch may have skipped those statements
notes: "A" (line 3) was not applied: a SET NOEXEC statement on line 5 in its batch can make SQL Server skip statements without an error. Put the SET statement in a batch of its own.
"B" (line 6) was not applied: a SET NOEXEC statement on line 5

cases.name: SET NOEXEC in a batch of its own leaves the next batch's names applied
a marker between GO and its count is in no batch: it is noted, not dropped
notes: "x" (line 2) is unused: no statement follows it in its batch.

cases.name: SET NOEXEC inside an IF applies no name: a GO 2 repetition starts with NOEXEC on
cases.sql:
-- #Name="A"
SELECT 1 AS a;
IF 1 = 1 BEGIN SET NOEXEC OFF; SELECT 9 AS z; SET NOEXEC ON; END
GO 2
notes: "A" (line 1) was not applied: a SET NOEXEC statement on line 3 in its batch can make SQL Server skip statements without an error.

cases.name: SET NOEXEC OFF inside an IF after an ON in an earlier batch applies no name
notes: "A" (line 3) was not applied: a SET NOEXEC statement on line 5 in its batch

cases.name: a SELECT aliased to the plan column is shown as a plan and not counted, so no name in its batch is applied
notes: "Saved plan" (line 1) was not applied: its batch names a column
"Stats" (line 3) was not applied: its batch names a column
